metadata.description: Epoch-1 artifact record (R8A2): the durable record of ONE artifact a build or package target produced — identity, kind, shape, placement, content digest, producer identity, freshness fingerprints, creation time and verification state (campaigns/packages-2026-09 architecture §4). A record states a fact about a run that already happened: it is not rebuildable from source, and it never carries credentials. Generated Rust is the runtime record type.
Record schema epoch; 1 in epoch 1. The behaviour cell refuses every other value, so a newer record fails loudly instead of parsing into a wrong meaning.

The stable artifact id — `vibe-helper.exe`, `vibe-helper.zip`. Obeys the one frozen backend-id grammar `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}`; validated by the behaviour cell, never normalised: a second id grammar would be a second thing to drift.

The absolute runtime placement, forward-slashed (`/…` or `X:/…`), control-free; validated by the behaviour cell in the same manner the trace report's run path is held. Paths are placement, never identity — `id` is the identity.

The safe project/slot/store-relative identity a later phase joins records by; validated by the behaviour cell against the project-relative path grammar (forward slashes, no `..`, no drive, no backslash).
The artifact's content witness: SHA-256 for a `file` shape, the canonical tree digest for a `directory` shape. A directory is a first-class artifact; it is not implicitly zipped.
Exactly which target, mechanism and provider produced the artifact — the row a freshness probe or a reproduction has to name.

The freshness fingerprints the engine recorded beside the artifact. The object is always present; each member is optional because a provider-fresh target may honestly lack one (Cargo owns inputs the engine does not model).
When the producing run created the artifact.
The verification verdict over the produced artifact, with its optional evidence summary. `unverified` is a legal, honest state — an unrun gate is never silently reported as run.
The media type of a `file`-shape artifact (`application/zip`, `text/markdown`); absent for a `directory` shape. Non-blank and control-free; validated by the behaviour cell.
The platform triple the artifact targets (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`); absent for a platform-independent artifact. Non-blank and control-free; validated by the behaviour cell.

A record's timestamp — a JTD `timestamp`, i.e. RFC 3339 on the wire, bound to `chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>` in code (the same binding the shared `timestamp` fragment and `hello`'s `world_sunset` carry). Spelled `"type": "timestamp"` and not `"type": "string"` because a bare string would give a date a SECOND legal spelling in the system, and one thing is written one way. Local to this schema: the record family is its only consumer, and a strict (`foreign_parsers = "none"`) schema must not pull a shared fragment the permissive formats also read.
The closed artifact-kind vocabulary of the §4 registry law. Growing it is a spec amendment, not a serde default — free-form kinds are exactly what the closed set refuses.
The physical shape on disk. `directory` says the artifact IS the tree the tree digest covers; `file` says it is the bytes the SHA-256 covers.

Which root `path` hangs from: the project tree, a workspace slot, or the content-addressed store. One closed vocabulary, because a relative identity that does not say which root it is relative to names nothing.
The safe relative identity: a named root plus a root-relative path. Later phases join records by this pair, never by rescanning a directory or guessing a filename.
The root `path` is relative to.
The root-relative path, forward-slashed, no `..`/`.`/empty segments, no drive prefix, no absolute root; validated by the behaviour cell through the shared project-relative path grammar.

The digest algorithm, spelled exactly as the architecture freezes it. `sha256` covers one file's bytes; `sha256-tree/1` covers a directory's canonical tree. Reopened only when acquire-role providers land.
One content witness: the algorithm plus its value.
Which digest this value is.
The digest itself — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters, no `sha256:` prefix (the algorithm member already names it); validated by the behaviour cell.
The exact provider behind a mechanism: the group-qualified key plus the version and content hash that make the identity reproducible.

The provider key in the ExtensionKey spelling `group/name#id` (the reserved builtin is `org.vibevm/vibe#cargo`). Exactly one `/` before exactly one `#`, every component non-blank; validated by the behaviour cell.
The provider's own version string; non-blank. Deliberately not parsed here — the provider registry owns its grammar.
The provider's content hash in the one identity spelling `sha256:` + 64 lowercase hex — the same form every lockfile row carries; validated by the behaviour cell.
What produced the artifact: the target that ran, the mechanism key it selected, and the exact provider identity that serviced it.
The producing target id — backend-id grammar; validated by the behaviour cell.

The role-qualified mechanism key (`build:cargo`, `package:agent-plugin`). The prefix must be one of the two producing families `build:`/`package:` (a deploy mechanism produces no artifact record; `acquire:` reopens with acquire-role providers), and the tail obeys the backend-id grammar; validated by the behaviour cell.
The exact provider identity — provider changes invalidate the target even when the logical mechanism name did not.

The three named freshness digests. Each is optional because a provider-fresh target may honestly lack one — an engine-side input census that Cargo does not own would be unsound, and absence is the honest record of that. All absent is the provider-fresh record.
The declared-input fingerprint — exactly 64 lowercase hex; validated by the behaviour cell.
The target-config fingerprint — exactly 64 lowercase hex; validated by the behaviour cell.
The toolchain fingerprint — exactly 64 lowercase hex; validated by the behaviour cell.
The verification verdict. `unverified` — the gate did not run; `verified` — it ran and passed; `failed` — it ran and refused.
The verification verdict with its optional evidence summary.
The verdict itself.

The evidence summary naming what proved the verdict; non-blank and control-free; validated by the behaviour cell. Absent for `unverified` and optional rather than required for the others, because the evidence kinds are the mechanism atom's to define.
